analysis: Examined the changes in EngineV2Bridge.swift (comment-only update at the stopStringScope doc, base/head lines 124-125; the head text shown is unrelated surrounding init code) and MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (patch plus base text). The scheduler change moves the reasoningPrefix computation before bridge.submitTokenized in the media path, and passes a per-request stopStringScope (ReasoningStopScope.scope(reasoningParser:reasoningPrefix:parsesToolCalls:)) into submitTokenized for the media path, the text path (~line 1044) and the cluster GLM path (~line 1428, reasoningPrefix nil). The reasoningPrefix computation is not new in the reasoning-parse sense: it was already computed after submit and is now just hoisted, with the redundant post-submit checkFirstContentDeadline calls removed. Error handling is unchanged: the outer catch still releases mediaGate and releaseBox, and the post-submit deadline check still cancels upstream. No new data egress, logging, or cache-scope/salt changes. cacheScope, cacheEnabled and hybridPrefixIdentity handling are untouched, so T-041 posture (coordinator-authored scope, SSD tier) is unaffected. Stop-string scope affects only output truncation semantics (client-supplied stop strings applied to reasoning vs content), not confidentiality or authorization, and the stopStringScope parameter on submitTokenized/bridge is outside the supplied evidence. Open integration questions: the implementation of ReasoningStopScope.scope and the bridge's handling of a per-request override versus the model default (not supplied); whether the removed second checkFirstContentDeadline between submit and stream creation leaves any gap (the one right after submit remains, so it appears safe). The head text of the text path at ~1044 was seen only in the patch. No concrete security regression identified.
